newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco plaintiff 'just sick' about settlement.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco plaintiff 'just sick' about settlement.

text.p: Norma Broin, the lead plaintiff in a landmark secondhand smoking lawsuit against the tobacco industry, said Friday she was "just sick" about the historic settlement between state attorneys general and the industry.
"This is just so wrong," Broin, 42, said in a telephone interview from her home in Stafford, Va. "This is just a fabulous, fabulous deal for the tobacco companies."

Broin, a non-smoker, launched a $5 billion class-action lawsuit against the tobacco industry on behalf of some 60,000 flight attendants who say they were sickened by breathing secondhand smoke on U.S. passenger jets.
Jury selection in the case, known as Broin vs. Philip Morris et al, began June 2 in Dade County, Fla., Circuit Court. The trial was expected to continue despite the settlement.
Broin said she believed lawsuits like hers had the tobacco industry on the run and there was nothing to be gained in the settlement, particularly now.

"There is absolutely no reason for the American public or the world public to make a deal with the devil," Broin said. "The ball is in our court. Obviously, if they (tobacco companies) are willing to negotiate, this is good for them."

Broin, who contracted lung cancer and sued the industry for damages six years ago, said the settlement threatened to undermine the rights of millions of Americans to have their day in court to seek damages for injuries suffered at the hands of the tobacco companies.
Broin called a promised $368.5 billion payment by the industry "no big deal."
"It's seven years' profits. So that means business as usual in seven years," she said.
